blocks.lead: The best vinyl plank for dogs is a rigid-core SPC plank with a 20 mil or thicker wear layer, a textured matte finish in a mid-tone color, and a waterproof core, installed with tight seams and a sealed transition at the door the dog uses. For dogs over about 70 lb, step up to a 28 mil commercial wear layer.
blocks.detail: That combination hides claw marks, survives accidents and sand from the beach, and still looks like wood. Wills Flooring installs vinyl plank for $2.50 per sq ft in labor, 500 sq ft minimum, $100 per stair.

blocks.html: Edmonds is a dog town. Between the off-leash beach at the marina, the trails at Yost Park and the walk-everywhere blocks of the Bowl, most of the houses we work in have at least one dog and a lot of them have two. The question owners ask, usually while a wet lab is shaking off in the entry, is which vinyl plank will actually stand up to that. A common Reddit thread lists a dozen brands. The brand matters less than five specs, and here they are in the order they matter.

blocks.text: What dogs actually do to a floor

items.title: Claws: thousands of micro-scratches
items.text: A dog's nails do not usually gouge a good vinyl plank. They leave a haze of fine scratches in the traffic lanes and where the dog skids to greet you at the door. On a glossy or very dark floor that haze shows as a dull path within months. On a textured matte plank in a mid-tone it is nearly invisible for years.

items.title: Accidents and water bowls
items.text: Urine, vomit and the puddle around the water bowl are the reason vinyl beats hardwood and laminate for dogs. A rigid vinyl core does not swell. The seams and the subfloor under them still can get wet, so a plank with tight locking joints and a quick cleanup habit are what keep the plywood underneath dry.

items.title: Sand, salt and grit
items.text: An Edmonds dog comes home from the beach carrying sand in its paws. Sand is harder than any wear layer and acts like sandpaper under the dog and under you. This is where wear layer thickness and a ceramic-bead or enhanced urethane coating earn their money, and where a good mat at the door does half the work.

items.title: Noise and traction
items.text: Nails on a hard, slick floor click all night and give older dogs nothing to push against. A plank with a textured surface and an attached pad quiets the clicking and gives a senior dog better footing. High-gloss smooth planks are the worst on both counts, whatever their wear layer.

blocks.title: Waterproof plank, not waterproof floor:
blocks.text: The plank will not swell, but a puddle left overnight still finds the seam and the plywood under it. In an older Edmonds rambler over a crawlspace that subfloor dries slowly and can smell for years. Wipe accidents when you find them, keep the water bowl on a tray, and use a plank with a tight locking system rather than the loosest click you can find.
Living with dogs on vinyl plank

items.html: Trim nails every two to three weeks. The most effective floor protection costs nothing. Long nails are what turn micro-scratches into visible scoring.
Sweep or vacuum sand daily in beach season. Grit under paws is the real enemy of the wear layer. A mat inside the door and a quick sweep beat any coating.
Use a pH-neutral cleaner. Vinegar, bleach and steam mops dull the coating and can void the warranty. A damp microfiber mop with a vinyl-safe cleaner is all it needs.
Put a washable rug where the dog lands. The spot in front of the couch and the bottom of the stairs take the impact. A rug with a non-staining backing saves those two spots.

Get the seams right the first time. Tight joints and a properly flat subfloor are an installation issue, not a product issue. Our vinyl plank installation comes with a 1-year workmanship warranty and a subfloor check at the estimate.

faq.q: Will dog nails scratch vinyl plank flooring?
faq.a: They will leave fine micro-scratches on any floor over time, but a 20 mil or thicker wear layer with a ceramic-bead or enhanced urethane coating resists them well, and a textured matte surface in a mid-tone hides the ones that occur. Glossy or very dark planks show nail haze within months. Regular nail trimming makes the biggest difference.

faq.q: What wear layer do I need for a large dog?
faq.a: For a dog over about 70 lb, or two or more active dogs, choose a 28 or 30 mil commercial-grade wear layer. A 20 mil plank handles a single medium dog well. Below 12 mil, expect visible wear paths in a year or two. Wills Flooring's install labor is $2.50 per sq ft at any wear layer.

faq.q: Is vinyl plank better than hardwood for dogs?
faq.a: For scratch and accident resistance, yes. Hardwood dents and scratches under claws and stains permanently from urine that soaks in; vinyl plank shrugs off both when cleaned reasonably promptly. Hardwood wins on resale and can be refinished, so many Edmonds owners put hardwood in formal rooms and vinyl plank where the dog lives.

faq.q: Is vinyl plank slippery for dogs?
faq.a: Smooth, glossy planks can be, especially for older dogs. A textured, embossed matte plank gives noticeably better traction, and an attached pad softens footfall. If you have a senior dog with hip trouble, choose the most textured surface you can find and add washable runners on the routes the dog uses most.

faq.q: What color vinyl plank hides dog hair and scratches best?
faq.a: Mid-tone browns and warm grays with visible grain variation. Solid dark planks show every light-colored hair and every scratch; very pale planks show dark fur and dirt. Variation in the print pattern breaks up both. Match the tone loosely to your dog's coat if one dog dominates the household.

faq.q: Does vinyl plank hold pet urine odor?
faq.a: The plank itself does not absorb odor. Odor comes from urine that reaches the subfloor through seams, which is why tight locking joints and quick cleanup matter more than the waterproof rating on the box. For a puppy or an incontinent senior dog, ask us about sealing the perimeter and transitions at installation.
